title: Devin Booker Hints at Potential Return to Seattle for The CrawsOver Pro-Am
htmlContent:
Devin Booker, the superstar of the Phoenix Suns, has expressed interest in playing at Seattle's well-known CrawsOver Pro-Am, one of basketball's most beloved summer events. Booker expressed his excitement about returning to the Pacific Northwest and playing under the guidance of his longtime mentor, Jamal Crawford, in an exclusive interview with LandonBuford.com. Booker responded without hesitation when asked if he would consider participating again this summer if the competition grew more intense.
“Heck yeah, I’ll pull up on J Crossover whenever — that’s my big brother.”
The wider hoops community and Seattle basketball fans were immediately captivated by his comments. Another exciting moment for a city that cherishes its basketball legacy would be if Booker appeared at The CrawsOver.

The CrawsOver: Seattle’s Summer Basketball Showcase

Jamal Crawford, the founder and host of The CrawsOver Pro-Am, has made it a cultural phenomenon and a showcase of elite basketball talent. The event takes place at Seattle Pacific University. It serves as a showcase for NBA players, overseas professionals, college stars, and local legends, all in a setting that combines high-level competition with the grassroots energy of community basketball. LeBron James, Jayson Tatum, Paolo Banchero, Dejounte Murray, Trae Young, and Zach LaVine are just some of the basketball icons who have appeared in The CrawsOver over the years. What was once a local pro-am league has now become a must-attend spectacle for fans and players, thanks to these appearances. The CrawsOver is more than just summer basketball for Seattle, which hasn't had an NBA franchise since the SuperSonics moved in 2008: the city's enduring basketball culture and its deep connections to the professional game.

Devin Booker and Jamal Crawford: A Brotherhood Beyond Basketball

Their connection is based on numerous shared values, including professionalism, creativity on the court, and a relentless passion for the game of basketball. The bond between the two is founded on mutual respect, mentorship, and love for the game.

Crawford, one of the NBA's most respected veterans and a Seattle native, has frequently praised Booker for his dedication and talent, describing him as one of the purest scorers of his generation.

Booker, for his part, has credited Crawford as one of the veterans who helped shape his mindset early in his career. Their connection is built on shared values — professionalism, creativity on the court, and a relentless passion for the game of basketball. When Booker calls Crawford “my big brother,” it's a recognition of Crawford's influence on him, both on and off the court, not just a nickname.

Seattle’s Basketball Renaissance

The relationship between Seattle and basketball is extensive. The city is renowned for consistently producing elite talent, from the Supersonics' 1979 NBA Championship to the rise of homegrown superstars such as Gary Payton, Brandon Roy, Nate Robinson, Isaiah Thomas, and Jamal Crawford. Seattle remains one of the most passionate basketball cities in the world, despite losing its NBA franchise. The city's basketball spirit has been kept alive by events such as The CrawsOver, which bring together players and fans to celebrate their love for the game. Bringing back Devin Booker would strengthen the connection between NBA stars and Seattle's basketball roots, highlighting the respect that players across the league have for the city and its basketball community.

The CrawsOver’s Impact on the Basketball Community

The CrawsOver has always placed a strong emphasis on accessibility and community, unlike many pro-am leagues. Fans of all ages and backgrounds can enjoy high-level basketball thanks to the free admission. Jamal Crawford's mission has always been clear: to give back to the city that gave him everything. Younger players have a unique chance to compete against NBA stars, gain exposure, and test their skills at an elite level. Stories, legends. For the community, it’s a gathering place—a space where stories and legends are celebrated, and the next generation of Seattle hoopsters is appreciated. Devin Booker returning to the CrawsOver court this summer would increase the event's visibility and reaffirm its position as one of the crown jewels of summer basketball.

Devin Booker: A Superstar Who Never Forgets His Roots

Fans are fond of Devin Booker because of his humility and connection to basketball's grassroots culture. Even though he has won three NBA All-Stars, won Olympic gold medals, and is one of the most dynamic scorers in the league, Booker consistently seeks to connect with the basketball community outside of the NBA spotlight. Booker keeps his focus on the game's essence, whether it's mentoring younger players, supporting AAU programs, or supporting events like The CrawsOver. He's open to playing in local pro-ams, which shows that basketball isn't just a career for him — it's a lifelong passion.

What Booker’s Return Would Mean for Seattle

If Booker makes good on his promise to come out for The CrawsOver, it would be a monumental moment for Seattle fans. The city's basketball community's strength would be further showcased by his presence, which is likely to attract massive crowds and create national buzz. In addition, Booker's presence would symbolise Seattle's ongoing importance in the basketball world, even without an NBA franchise. Jamal Crawford's contribution to fostering unity and opportunity through basketball would also be another reminder.

Conclusion: A Brotherhood, A City, and a Game That Unites All

Devin Booker’s statement — “Heck yeah, I’ll pull up on J Crossover whenever, that’s my big brother," captures more than just a casual remark. What makes The CrawsOver unique is its brotherhood, respect, and shared love for the game, all captured in this message. Booker's potential return to Seattle this summer would be a homecoming of sorts, a celebration of basketball culture, mentorship, and community spirit. Devin Booker's game and character are still inspiring fans and players, regardless of where they are. The CrawsOver remains more than an event — it's a reminder that basketball's heart beats strongest in places where players play for love, not for lights. Devin Booker's return to Seattle will be met with open arms by the city.
